Per-agent model tiers: Opus (architect, deep design), Sonnet (builder, inspector, librarian), Haiku (ops, scout, scribe, tester).
All hooks, the supervisor, the self-audit, reconciliation + migration scripts, and the docx generators.

permissions (bypassPermissions) + SessionEnd/SubagentStop hook wiring; SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks wired in the global ~/.claude config.

QI_ NSSM services are supervised (not owned) here; QI_ClaudeSelfAudit and QI_ClaudeVoiceMeeting_8AM scheduled tasks drive monthly + daily automation.
qi_brain.db is the reconciliation + session target; the librarian queries its docs/doc_relationships catalog and the qi_docs Chroma collection.
Live snapshot at session start (HTTP) and qi.* MCP tools (get_context, log_session, log_decision, search_memory).
Single source for every project's path, ports, status, and relationships — read by the supervisor and both hooks for project inference.

descriptions.title: A management workspace, not a served app
descriptions.body: Claude Manager (claude_manager, C:\CLAUDE) is registered family_tier=backbone with no served ports — its own registry note reads 'Management/meta workspace that operates ON the ecosystem rather than being a deployed app.' Everything here acts on other projects: it scans them, reconciles their Brain records, ingests their sessions, and dispatches work into them. The 'tech stack' is therefore deliberately glue: the Claude Code harness, Python/PowerShell automation, the registry, the Brain, and Windows process/service control. It is the difference between the engine room (C:\QIH) and the bridge from which the engine room is commanded.

descriptions.title: Why eight agents and a dispatch rule
descriptions.body: Claude Code does not auto-route work to sub-agents — DISPATCH_PROTOCOL.md is explicit that 'if I don't dispatch, no one does.' So the fabric is a discipline encoded in two places: the eight .md agent definitions (each pinning a role, a model tier, and an allowed tool set) and the protocol that maps task triggers to agents and chains them into workflows (design->build->review->document). The model tiers are the cost lever: Opus only for architecture, Sonnet for code and review, Haiku for the high-frequency ops/scout/scribe/tester work. The main thread stays the orchestrator, delegation is kept one level deep, and attribution is honest — a sub-agent's work is logged as that agent, not as the main thread.

descriptions.title: The supervisor: registry in, three artifacts out
descriptions.body: supervisor.py is the drift engine. It reads qi_registry.json, then for every project checks five things — does the path exist, is git clean (untracked vs modified counts, last-commit age), are there keepalive *failure-state*.json files, are its QI_ NSSM services running, and did its scheduled tasks exit non-zero. Each finding is severity-tagged and rolled up to red/yellow/green. It emits three artifacts: a human DASHBOARD.md, a machine report.json, and an update into C:\QIH\data\status.json that lights up the QI Hive dashboard panels. The service/task probes shell out to PowerShell over nssm.exe and Get-ScheduledTask, matched by AppDirectory/action path so only services genuinely rooted under the project count.

descriptions.title: Hooks: guaranteeing the session is never silent
descriptions.body: Three hook scripts make memory automatic. SessionStart (session_context.py, wired globally) injects the ecosystem briefing, a live Brain probe that fails LOUD if Brain is down, the dispatch reminder, and the monthly-audit review gate. SessionEnd (session_end.py, wired in this project's settings.json) writes a session stub to the Hive inbox so QI_HiveIngest records it in qi_brain.db even when Claude forgot to log explicitly — inferring the project from cwd via longest-prefix match against the registry (with C:\CLAUDE falling through to claude_manager). SubagentStop (subagent_stop.py) does the same for each sub-agent, normalising its name to hive_<role> so cross-project memory is attributed correctly. All three are best-effort and never block the session.

descriptions.title: Safe-by-design automation
descriptions.body: The self-audit and the restart guard share a philosophy: only ever auto-do what is provably reversible or provably orphaned. qi_self_audit.py --apply-safe is limited to killing orphaned MCP processes, removing git worktrees with a clean working tree, and pruning dead .claude.json entries (with a timestamped backup); everything else — large folders, temp files, backup accumulation — is reported into PENDING_REVIEW.json for the in-session decision gate. The restart guard's kill-set is built from claude.exe descendant trees plus MCP-signature orphans, but Is-UnderService explicitly excludes anything parented by services.exe/nssm/svchost so the QI_ tunnels and Brain API are never collateral, and it removes its own ancestor chain so running it from inside a session can't kill the host.

descriptions.title: One source of truth, read everywhere
descriptions.body: Nothing in this workspace hardcodes a path or a port. The supervisor, both inbox hooks, and the reconciliation scripts all read C:\QIH\ecosystem\qi_registry.json to learn where projects live and which ports they own. This is what lets a project move (FileHQ absorbed into Naya, UNIVERSAL into QIH) or a port change (Brain 9010->9011) propagate without editing the tooling — the one known exception being the SessionStart hook's still-hardcoded :9010 Brain probe, which is on the roadmap to repoint.
